acceptance_probes.procedure: Existing account starts native authorization, authenticates at existing GALX portal, consents, exchanges a one-use PKCE code and receives audience/scope-restricted authorization. Browser session alone, malformed/expired/wrong-audience/missing-scope tokens, no entitlement, another client and replayed code/refresh must be denied with zero new upstream dispatch.
acceptance_probes.evidence: HTTP status and public error code, grant ID, client ID, entitlement decision; never raw credentials.

acceptance_probes.procedure: One tiny streamed request with a unique request key and bounded output; verify admission, exactly one upstream execution, sanitized events and honest terminal outcome. A genuine unknown is recorded without replay; successful real inference remains a required acceptance proof.
acceptance_probes.evidence: Nova request ID -> private execution ID, provider-attempt count, terminal state and result hash, not prompt/credential dumps.

acceptance_probes.procedure: After receiving real stream output, cancel once. Confirm caller interruption/terminal unknown and unchanged provider failure count; wait for settlement and prove no subsequent dispatch for that original key.
acceptance_probes.evidence: Before/after account failure count and execution record; cancellation is neutral, not a health test.

acceptance_probes.procedure: Resubmit the identical private runtime request key/fingerprint to the existing execution, proving attachment and a single upstream attempt. At the public Nova boundary the same submitted request key returns the established 409 request_already_submitted with prior outcome; it must not create a new upstream execution. Do not change either established contract to manufacture a streamed replay.
acceptance_probes.evidence: Original execution identity retained, dispatch count unchanged; both boundary responses recorded.

acceptance_probes.procedure: Keep independently consented browser client active. Disconnect native, timestamp committed acknowledgement with a monotonic clock, immediately request new admission and refresh using that connection, then verify browser client and GALX Media remain usable.
acceptance_probes.contract: Every new admission/refresh after disconnect acknowledgement must fail; existing shared row-lock checks have no propagation cache. Requests admitted earlier may finish. Measure request round-trip separately; do not use historical 175 ms as an SLA.
acceptance_probes.evidence: Acknowledgement/admission times, denial status, measured elapsed ms, independent client result and unchanged completed records.

acceptance_probes.procedure: Use the single user and at most two concurrent small requests across its two clients; a third admission must return service_busy without a provider attempt. Cancel/settle once and respect the retained unknown reservation deadline. No destructive or provider-quota exhaustion load.
acceptance_probes.evidence: Configured caps, active slot counts, third-call denial, unchanged login/grant and provider-health counters.

acceptance_probes.procedure: Authenticated local monitor reads current private control ownership, while browser status contains only its documented DTO fields. Anonymous monitor access remains denied. Inspect response headers, raw bodies, streams, SDK errors, browser/native logs and delivered assets for keys/private IDs/topology.
acceptance_probes.evidence: Field allowlists and redacted artifact hashes. Whole live-site cleanliness is not claimed by this preflight.

acceptance_probes.procedure: Before declaring target acceptance, validate interruption at the target execution limit without replay. Current Vercel Hobby Fluid maximum and route maxDuration are 300 s; executor wall limit is also 300 s. Outer-host termination can precede cleanup, so record the actual client/durable state and six-minute reservation behavior; do not infer a guaranteed terminal update from local cancellation tests.
acceptance_probes.evidence: Target-produced interruption evidence or an explicit unresolved acceptance blocker; no timeout semantics change authorized.

Drain in-flight work or record an unconfirmed interruption without replay; verify pending settlement and ownership. If exposure occurred, close the exposed path first and contain compromised credentials through a separately scoped incident action.

Remove candidate route/alias exposure. Restore the recorded previous Vercel deployment only if an alias was changed; preserve GALX Media aliases throughout a private candidate deployment. Never rebuild old source to approximate rollback.

Restore prior runtime/monitor image IDs and exact baseline configuration/mounts using the local service procedure and 61-second owner handoff. Central authority/proxy normally stays unchanged. Do not downgrade to pre-neutral runtime or migration.

Retain new additive quota state with old compatible services. If quota function is corrupt, use the reviewed fail-closed DOWN transaction as containment and keep inference closed pending forward repair.
Verify media reachability, old runtime/monitor health, private ownership, sanitized browser status, zero unexpected new attempts and intact execution digest; keep cohort closed.
rollback.transition: Media need not be interrupted when its serving alias stays unchanged. Replacing the single local runtime pauses inference; drain time plus at least 61 seconds ownership fencing and startup/readiness delay apply. No measured recovery-time guarantee is claimed.
